title: Repeats in a Family
statement: Let $P(x)=x^2-31x+198$ and $Q(x)=x^2-27x+170$. There are exactly two real numbers $\lambda$ for which the polynomial $P(x)+\lambda Q(x)$ has a repeated real root. Let $r_1$ and $r_2$ be the repeated roots corresponding to these two values of $\lambda$. Find $r_1^2+r_2^2$.
hints: Look at the one member of the family that is not quadratic: taking $\lambda=-1$ gives $P(x)-Q(x)$, which is linear. Find its root, then evaluate $P$ and $Q$ at that point.

The root of $P-Q$ is $x=7$, and $P(7)=Q(7)=30$. Make the variable substitution $u=x-7$, so that $P$ and $Q$ have the same constant term in $u$. Then consider what Vieta's formula for the product of the roots says about every quadratic member of the family.

With $u=x-7$, we have $P+\lambda Q=(1+\lambda)(u^2+30)-(17+13\lambda)u$. For $\lambda\ne -1$ the product of the roots in $u$ is $30$, so a repeated root satisfies $u^2=30$. Convert these values of $u$ back to $x$.
solution: We have $P(x)-Q(x)=-4x+28$, which vanishes at $x=7$, and $P(7)=Q(7)=30$. This suggests putting $u=x-7$, which gives $$P=u^2-17u+30,\qquad Q=u^2-13u+30.$$ Therefore $$P+\lambda Q=(1+\lambda)(u^2+30)-(17+13\lambda)u.$$ If $\lambda=-1$, this equals $-4u$, which has a single simple root, so there is no repeated root. If $\lambda\ne -1$, the polynomial is a quadratic in $u$ whose roots have product $30$ by Vieta's formulas. A repeated root $u_0$ therefore satisfies $u_0^2=30$, so $u_0=\sqrt{30}$ or $u_0=-\sqrt{30}$. Each of these values does occur, and for exactly one $\lambda$. The polynomial equals $(1+\lambda)(u-u_0)^2$ exactly when $17+13\lambda=2u_0(1+\lambda)$, that is, when $(13-2u_0)\lambda=2u_0-17$. Since $2u_0$ is irrational, $13-2u_0\ne 0$, so this has exactly one solution $\lambda$. That solution is not $-1$, because $\lambda=-1$ would give $17+13\lambda=4$ but $2u_0(1+\lambda)=0$. Hence the two values of $\lambda$ correspond to the two values $u_0=\pm\sqrt{30}$. Returning to $x=u+7$, the repeated roots are $r_1=7+\sqrt{30}$ and $r_2=7-\sqrt{30}$. Therefore $$r_1^2+r_2^2=2(7^2+30)=158.$$ The answer is $158$. Why this works. pencil-of-curves, variable-substitution, vieta: recentring at the root of the family's linear member gives every quadratic member the same product of roots, which forces the possible repeated roots.
